strengths: The paper addresses an important explanatory question: why categorical distributional RL can outperform methods that estimate expected returns. Its decomposition offers an interpretable perspective on the role of distributional information.

The basic mixture identity and cross-entropy decomposition are transparent, with an explicit validity condition. The related-work discussion engages relevant research on distributional learning, optimization, statistical efficiency, and exploration.

The experiments cover Atari and continuous control, include categorical and quantile critics and atom-count ablations, and report multiple seeds with standard deviations. Reporting both beneficial and adverse interactions with policy entropy is useful.
weaknesses: The central exploration claim is not established. Equation (4) decomposes a loss used to fit the critic, whereas Equations (7)-(9) introduce an additional reward bonus through an arbitrary increasing function. No equivalence to ordinary C51 or DSAC policy updates is derived. Theorem 1 concerns a constructed reward-augmented problem with q held fixed, rather than establishing the claimed intrinsic exploration mechanism.

The main ablation does not isolate the proposed regularizer. Section 6.1 trains against the residual distribution μ instead of the original target p. Equation (43) shows that lowering the ratio ε removes probability from the bin containing the mean and redistributes it elsewhere; it does not approach a target concentrated at the mean or recover DQN/SAC. Performance degradation can therefore reflect target distortion and altered optimization rather than removal of an exploration benefit.

Cross-entropy does not measure distributional mismatch alone: H(μ,q) = H(μ) + KL(μ||q). It can remain large when q equals μ, so a large bonus need not indicate misestimated uncertainty. This undermines the interpretation that the bonus specifically directs policies toward states whose return distributions are poorly estimated.

Proposition 3 relates idealized limiting minimizers, leaving the connection to finite-bin neural learning dynamics unresolved. There are also concrete proof errors: Equation (39) yields Θ(Δ), not o(Δ), and Appendix G incorrectly invokes Banach's fixed-point theorem using only a non-expansive KL bound.

The experiments measure returns without directly testing the proposed exploration mechanism. State-visitation measurements, return-distribution estimation errors, or controlled environments varying environmental noise would help distinguish exploration from representation and optimization effects. The reported improvement or interference from combining entropy terms is compatible with these alternative explanations.

Reproducibility is partial. Appendix K provides useful hyperparameters, but C51 support ranges and the Atari preprocessing, exploration, and evaluation protocols are not clearly specified. Code is promised after acceptance, leaving these implementation choices difficult to verify from the manuscript.
